phase1.output: (Window appears with all controls: Label, Button, TextField, TextArea, CheckBox, RadioButtons, ComboBox, ListView, Slider, ProgressBar, etc.)
phase1.explanation:
This lesson doesn't teach a new idea so much as it stocks the shelves — a tour of the actual [[term:controls]] a customer can touch: the merchandise, not the shelving. You've been using Label and Button since 5.2; this lesson rounds out the rest of the catalog.

TextField takes a single line of typed input; TextArea takes several. Both support setPromptText("..."), the faint gray placeholder text that disappears the moment someone starts typing — [[key:prompt text is a hint, not a value]]; getText() on an untouched field returns an empty string, not the prompt. CheckBox is a simple on/off toggle via setSelected(). RadioButton is trickier — on its own it behaves like a checkbox, but [[warn:radio buttons only become mutually exclusive once you assign them to the same ToggleGroup]]; skip that step and a user could select three "exclusive" options at once.

ComboBox and ListView both hold a collection of items (getItems().addAll(...)), but they display differently — ComboBox collapses to one visible row until clicked, ListView shows several rows at once, scrollable. Slider and ProgressBar both represent a value along a range, one draggable, one read-only. And Tooltip is the one control that isn't really its own shelf item — you attach it to another control with setTooltip(), and it only appears on hover.

[[fun:none of these controls need to be styled or wired to do anything yet]] — that's next lesson (events) and the one after (CSS). Right now the goal is just knowing the catalog: what each control is for, and which method sets its value.

phase2.explanation:
[[warn:the window opens completely empty]] — same failure mode as the layout lessons, for the same root cause.

Creating a control and adding it to root.getChildren() are two separate steps, and skipping the second one is invisible at compile time — every control here is a perfectly valid object, [[key:it just never gets attached to anything the Scene actually renders]]. The broken version constructs a VBox and a handful of controls but never once calls getChildren().add() or addAll() on the VBox, so the Scene wraps a container that's technically there and visually empty.

phase3.openingDialogue: Controls — the building blocks of your UI! 🧱

mcq.question:
You create three RadioButtons for a "pick one" question but forget to call setToggleGroup() on any of them. What actually happens when a user clicks all three?

A) A compile error — RadioButtons require a ToggleGroup to be constructed
B) Only the first one stays selected, the rest are automatically deselected
C) All three stay selected at once, because nothing is enforcing exclusivity between them
D) A runtime exception the moment the second one is clicked

phase4.selfChallenge:
Write a JavaFX program that:
1. Creates a VBox with spacing 15 and padding 20
2. Adds a Label "User Registration"
3. Adds a TextField with prompt "Enter username"
4. Adds a TextField with prompt "Enter password" (use PasswordField)
5. Adds a CheckBox "Remember me"
6. Adds a ComboBox with "Student", "Teacher", "Staff"
7. Adds a Button "Register"
8. Shows the window

phase5.trivia: [[fun:TextField and TextArea both descend from a common TextInputControl class]], which is why prompt text, editability, and basic text-selection behavior work identically on both — TextArea just adds multi-line wrapping and a scrollbar on top of the same foundation.
